questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hjFkjH on main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved project views).
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules, so that requests like "review my diff" or "why is this broken" automatically route to the right skill. This is a one-time setup prompt per project. Note: plan mode is active, so if you pick A the append and commit happen after the review finishes and plan mode exits.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Low either way; without routing you invoke skills by name manually.
Recommendation: A because routing rules make later sessions faster with zero downside for a fixture repo.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: convenience of auto-routing vs. keeping CLAUDE.md untouched.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description:
Append the standard gstack skill-routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit it once plan mode exits.
✅ Future requests auto-route to /investigate, /review, /ship etc. without remembering names
✅ Standard block, identical across gstack projects; easy to remove later
❌ Adds ~20 lines to CLAUDE.md and one commit to a repo that is currently a single-file fixture

options.label: No thanks, invoke manually
options.description:
Record routing_declined=true so this prompt never fires again for this project.
✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as checked in; no extra commit
✅ Re-enable any time with gstack-config set routing_declined false
❌ You type skill names yourself every time

questions.question:
D2 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hjFkjH on main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved project views).
ELI10: gstack logs small lessons (command quirks, pitfalls) per project. With cross-project search on, reviews in this repo can also pull lessons learned in your other projects on this machine. Everything stays local; nothing leaves the machine. Recommended for solo developers. Skip if you work across multiple client codebases where mixing context is a concern.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Minor; either setting is a one-line config flip later.
Recommendation: A because more prior learnings means fewer repeated mistakes, and the data stays on your machine.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: broader recall vs. strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description:
Set cross_project_learnings=true; learnings search spans all local projects.
✅ Patterns found in other repos (e.g. migration pitfalls) surface in this review
✅ Local only; no network, no data leaves the machine
❌ Client-codebase contexts could bleed together if you consult for multiple orgs

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description:
Set cross_project_learnings=false; only this project's learnings are searched.
✅ Strict isolation between codebases
✅ Nothing from unrelated projects influences this review
❌ Repeats lessons already learned elsewhere on this machine

questions.question:
D3 — MODE: Which review posture should I take on the saved project views plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hjFkjH on main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved views: table + CRUD + picker).
ELI10: A review mode sets how hard I push on scope. Expansion means I pitch a bigger, better product. Selective means I keep your scope and offer add-ons one at a time for you to take or leave. Hold means I do not touch scope and go deep on failure modes, tests and edge cases. Reduction means I look for what to cut. This plan adds a capability to an existing task list (an enhancement) at roughly 12 files (estimate), which is under the cut threshold.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too ambitious and you ship a bigger surface than the pilot needs; too narrow and the view scope model and filter serialization get locked in a shape that costs a migration later.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because this is an enhancement to a live system with two cheap-now, expensive-later design forks (shared views, canonical filter state) that deserve an explicit yes/no rather than silent omission or a full cathedral pitch.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how much I push scope vs. how much I harden what is already there.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description:
Hold the current scope and run the HOLD checks, then offer each expansion (shared/team views, URL-shareable view links, default view per project, stale-filter handling, usage metrics) individually with effort and risk. You accept, defer, or skip each one.
✅ Surfaces the two lock-in decisions (scope model, serialization) as explicit choices before code exists
✅ Nothing enters scope without your yes; rejected items land in NOT in scope with a reason
❌ More questions than HOLD; expect 4–6 cherry-pick prompts before the deep review starts

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description:
Dream big: pitch the 10x version (views as a first-class platform: shared, default, linkable, pinned, with analytics) and recommend each piece enthusiastically.
✅ Best if you want the platonic ideal of views laid out before you build anything
✅ Catches adjacent delighters a narrow review would never raise
❌ For a two-week pilot of a filter-saving feature this is likely more surface than the team needs to learn from

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description:
Keep exactly the four approach bullets; go maximum depth on error paths, access control, race conditions, tests, observability and rollout for that scope only.
✅ Fastest path to an implementable, hardened plan for the pilot
✅ Zero scope negotiation; every question is about correctness
❌ Per-member-only scoping and the serialization shape get baked in without a deliberate decision

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description:
Propose the minimum core (e.g. remember last filter per member, or URL-state only) and ask per item what to defer.
✅ Smallest possible diff for the pilot
✅ Tests the premise cheaply before investing in CRUD + picker
❌ "Named views you can reopen" is already close to minimum; cutting further changes the goal, not just the scope

questions.question:
D4.0 — Nine expansion proposals are pending (E1 canonical filter state, E2 shared project views, E3 project default view, E4 shareable links, E5 stale-reference resilience, E6 Save/Save-as/Revert, E7 instrumentation + baseline, E8 auto-restore last view, E9 picker polish bundle). How should I walk them past you?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hjFkjH on main, SCOPE EXPANSION review of saved project views.
ELI10: Each proposal is an independent yes/no on scope, so the default is one question per item (nine short prompts, each with Add / Defer / Skip / Hold). That is a lot of clicks but every item gets your explicit call, and dependencies (E3 needs E2; E4, E5, E8 lean on E1) get surfaced as we go. Alternatively I can propose a smaller set first, or batch them into groups.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Batching hides individual items behind group picks; narrowing first means I pre-filter your decision space, which is the exact thing scope expansion mode is meant to avoid.
Recommendation: A because every item is independent and you chose the mode that wants the full menu on the table.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: nine explicit decisions vs. fewer prompts with less granularity.

options.label: Full split, one per item (recommended)
options.description:
Fire D4.1 through D4.9 sequentially, then D4.final to confirm the assembled scope.
✅ Every proposal gets its own Add / Defer / Skip / Hold call with its dependency spelled out
✅ Hold on any item stops the chain so we can discuss before continuing
❌ Nine prompts before the deep review begins (each is a single click)

options.label: Narrow first
options.description:
I propose a smaller set (my pick: E1, E2, E5, E6, E7) and ask about only those; the rest go to NOT in scope as skipped-by-narrowing with a note.
✅ Roughly half the prompts
✅ Focuses on the lock-in and zero-silent-failure items
❌ I pre-filter your options, which cuts against the scope expansion posture you chose

options.label: Batch into groups
options.description:
Three grouped questions: foundation (E1, E5, E7), sharing (E2, E3, E4), personal UX (E6, E8, E9), each with multi-select.
✅ Three prompts instead of nine
✅ Groups follow real dependency lines
❌ Defer vs Skip per item is lost; groups get one disposition unless you type overrides
